The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY). A component's
  rules include those of the patterns and guidelines it follows, at their own addresses (for
  example `pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit`).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names. Once per project, read `setup --impl <name>` (MCP: `setup`)
  for what every component shares: installing the package, loading its styles, and fonts.
- Components style only themselves. Before building a page, `get guideline.page-setup` for the
  page's base font, text color, background, and heading recipes, and load the base stylesheet it
  names when your technology has one.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

$ taproot setup --impl web
# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

$ taproot get guideline.page-setup
# Page setup

Set the page's base font, text color, background, and heading type from semantic tokens, because components style only themselves.

The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.

## Rules

### Behavior

- **MUST** load-tokens: Load the token package once, at the root of the page, before any component renders. Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type.
- **MUST** page-base-text: The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color.
- **MUST** page-background: The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it.
- **SHOULD** heading-recipes: Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level.
- **SHOULD** base-stylesheet: Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation.
- **MUST** no-guessed-names: Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead.

## Links

### related

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

$ taproot get component.radio-group --impl web
# Radio group

Use Radio group to choose exactly one option from a short visible list.

A labeled set of mutually exclusive options with a shared hint and error. Choosing an option unchecks the previous one.

## When to use

- Choose one delivery method or plan from a short list.

## When not to use

- Choose any number of independent options. Use [Checkbox](component.checkbox) instead. Radio options are mutually exclusive.
- Choose from a long list. Use [Select](component.select) instead. A compact picker makes a long list easier to scan.
- Switch which view of the same subject is shown, without saving a choice. Use [Tabs](component.tabs) instead. Tabs change what is shown. A radio group records a value.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Group label and choices and messages. |
| label | label | Visible group name. |
| options | container | Ordered collection of the choices. |
| choice | container | One radio control and its visible option label. |
| control | interactive-surface | Circular selection control. |
| indicator | indicator | Dot appears inside the checked control. |
| option-label | label | Visible name of one option. |
| hint | description | Shared supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Shared message describing what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible accessible name of the group. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance associated with the group. |
| error | string |  |  | Nonempty text marks the group invalid and blocks submission. |
| name | string |  |  | Field name used for submission. |
| value | string |  |  | Checked option value. Empty means no option is checked. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Makes all options unavailable. |
| required | boolean |  | `false` | Requires one enabled option before submission. |

## Events

- `input`: Selection changed from user interaction.
- `change`: Selection committed from user interaction.

## Items

### choice

Options of each `choice`.

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible name of the option, and its accessible name. Required. |
| value | string |  |  | Identifies the option. Nonempty and unique within the group; the value parameter checks the option whose value it matches. |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Makes this option unavailable, while the others stay available. |

## States

`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `checked`, `disabled`, `invalid`

## Rules

Includes the rules of pattern.form-field, guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **MUST** unique-options: Each option has a visible label and a unique nonempty value. The group has a visible label.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#visible-label: Provide a visible label that names the value. Placeholder text is not a label.
  - Do: Email address
  - Avoid: Enter email
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#hint-adds-information: Use a hint only for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-says-what-to-fix: Write the error as what to fix.
  - Do: Enter an email address with an @ sign
  - Avoid: Invalid
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#explain-disabled: When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.

### Behavior

- **MUST** exclusive-choice: Choosing an option unchecks any other. Activating the checked option keeps it checked.
- **MUST** selection-events: User selection changes report input then change. Programmatic changes report neither.
- **MUST** disabled-options: Disabled options cannot be checked by pointer or keyboard. Disabled groups prevent all interaction.
- **SHOULD** form-value: The checked option's value submits under the group name, and nothing submits when no option is checked. Reset restores the initially checked option.
  - Extends: pattern.form-field#form-value
  - Applies when: The control belongs to a form.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-marks-invalid: A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#clear-error: Clear the error when the person edits the value, and on form reset, which restores the value but leaves the error.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit: While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#required-blocks-submit: A required control with no value blocks its form from submitting.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-prevents-interaction: Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-submits-nothing: A disabled control submits nothing.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** accessible-group: Associate the group label and hint and error with the options. Expose each option name and checked state.
- **MUST** keyboard-selection: Tab enters and leaves the group. Arrow keys move focus and the checked option between enabled options and wrap at either end. Space checks the focused option.
- **MUST** forced-colors: A checked dot and visible keyboard focus remain distinguishable under forced colors.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#label-is-name: The visible label is the control's accessible name.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#described-by-hint-and-error: The hint and the error are associated with the control, so assistive technology reads them as its description.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#invalid-not-color-alone: The invalid state always includes the error text, so meaning never depends on color alone.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#required-announced: A required control is announced as required, and shows it by more than color.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.

## Accessibility

- Role: Radio group
- Name: From the visible group label. Each option has its own visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Enter or leave the group using the checked enabled option or the platform entry option when none is checked. |
| Arrow keys | Move focus and selection between enabled options with wrapping. |
| Space | Select the focused option. |

## Rationale

- **Choices are items, and each choice owns its label, value, and availability.** Each choice carries a label, a value, and whether it is unavailable, so they are options of the choice, not of the whole group (ADR 0004). The group's disabled parameter makes every choice unavailable at once.
- **One size and vertical layout with no density or icon-only option.** A small circular control and visible label suit short lists. The dot is centered in the control. Both sizes are in the token map as spacing primitives, because no semantic size role exists (tokens ADR 0003). Layout around the group controls density.
- **No mixed or loading state.** Exactly one option can be checked and a form applies the choice later.
- **No animation or reduced motion variation.** Selection updates immediately.
- **Option order follows the inline direction in right-to-left layouts.** Labels follow their controls and directional keyboard behavior follows platform conventions.
- **Consume semantic colors and typography with the semantic pill radius.** Radio circles need the semantic pill radius.
- **Disabled colors override checked and invalid colors while the checked dot stays visible.** The group communicates availability and the checked option together.
- **No visited state and spacing consumes existing primitives.** Selection does not track navigation history. The system has no semantic spacing roles for choice rows.
- **Checked and invalid borders take precedence over hover.** Hover strengthens only the unchecked valid control. Checked and invalid together retain the checked background with the danger border.

## Links

### alternative

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Choose any number of independent options. Radio options are mutually exclusive.
- [Select](component.select) — Choose from a long list. A compact picker makes a long list easier to scan.
- [Tabs](component.tabs) — Switch which view of the same subject is shown, without saving a choice. Tabs change what is shown. A radio group records a value.

### alternative-to

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Choose exactly one option from a list. Checkboxes are independent. Nothing stops two being checked.
- [Select](component.select) — Show a short list of choices for comparison. Radio group keeps every choice visible.
- [Switch](component.switch) — Choose one item from a list. A switch represents one independent setting.
- [Tabs](component.tabs) — Choose a value that is saved or submitted with a form. Tabs change what is shown, not what is stored. A radio group records the choice.

### follows

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)
- [Form field](pattern.form-field)

### related

- [Checkbox](component.checkbox)
- [Tabs](component.tabs)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-radio-group>`

### Import

```js
import { defineRadioGroup } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/radio-group";

defineRadioGroup();
```

### Usage

```html
<ds-radio-group label="Delivery method" name="delivery" value="standard" required>
  <option value="standard">Standard delivery</option>
  <option value="express">Express delivery</option>
</ds-radio-group>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | parameter `label` | string | Visible accessible name of the group. |
| `hint` | attribute | parameter `hint` | string | Supporting guidance associated with the group. |
| `error` | attribute | parameter `error` | string | Nonempty text marks the group invalid and blocks submission. |
| `name` | attribute | parameter `name` | string | Field name used for submission. |
| `value` | attribute | parameter `value` | string | Checked option value. Empty means no option is checked. |
| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean | Makes all options unavailable. |
| `required` | attribute | parameter `required` | boolean | Requires one enabled option before submission. |
| `input` | event | event `input` |  | Selection changed from user interaction. |
| `change` | event | event `change` |  | Selection committed from user interaction. |
| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

### Choice element: `<option>`

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | property | choice parameter `label` | string | The option's text. A label attribute, when present, replaces the text as the label. |
| `value` | attribute | choice parameter `value` | string | Identifies the option. Nonempty and unique within the group; the value parameter checks the option whose value it matches. |
| `disabled` | attribute | choice parameter `disabled` | boolean | Makes this option unavailable, while the others stay available. |

Supply direct native `option` children with unique nonempty `value` attributes and visible text.
An option's `disabled` attribute makes it unavailable. The group creates native radio inputs in
one shadow root, so browser keyboard navigation and mutual exclusion remain native.

The `value` attribute sets the initial selection. Read or set the `value` property for the live
selection. Form reset restores the attribute. Children can be added, removed, or updated after
connection. An unmatched value selects nothing. A selected disabled option submits nothing and
does not satisfy `required`.

Tokens: 44 bindings, left out here. Run `taproot tokens component.radio-group` to filter them by part, condition, or property.
Setup: install, styles, and fonts are the same for every component. Run `taproot setup --impl web` once per project.


$ taproot get component.checkbox --impl web
# Checkbox

Use Checkbox to turn one independent option on or off, with a label, hint, and error.

Turns one independent option on or off, and associates a label, optional hint, and optional error with the control.

## When to use

- Turn one option on or off in a form that is submitted later.
- Choose any number of options from a short list, one checkbox per option.
- Confirm an agreement or acknowledgement before submit.
- Select or clear a list of options at once, showing indeterminate when only some are selected.

## When not to use

- Choose exactly one option from a list. Use [Radio group](component.radio-group) instead. Checkboxes are independent. Nothing stops two being checked.
- Apply a setting as soon as it is toggled, with no submit. Use [Switch](component.switch) instead. A checkbox value takes effect when its form is submitted.
- Trigger an action by itself. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Checkbox records a choice.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | The choice row, then hint and error, stacked together. |
| choice | container | Box and label side by side. The whole row is the click target. |
| control | interactive-surface | The box. Owns checked state and focus. |
| indicator | indicator | Check mark when checked, dash when indeterminate. Drawn inside the box and hidden from assistive technology. |
| label | label | Visible name for the option. |
| hint | description | Optional supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Optional message that says what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| error | string |  |  | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the control invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| checked | boolean |  | `false` | Whether the option is on. The value given at creation is the initial state that reset restores. |
| indeterminate | boolean |  | `false` | Shows a mixed state, for a parent whose options are partly selected. Presentational only; it does not change the submitted value. |
| name | string |  |  | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name when checked. |
| value | string |  |  | Value submitted when checked. Defaults to "on". |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` | Prevents toggling. A disabled checkbox does not submit its value. |
| required | boolean |  | `false` | The checkbox must be checked before submit. Conveyed by more than color. |

## Events

- `input`: The checked state changed from user interaction.
- `change`: The checked state was committed from user interaction.

## States

`disabled`, `invalid`, `indeterminate`, `checked`, `hover`, `focus`, `default`

## Rules

Includes the rules of pattern.form-field, guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **SHOULD** label-states-positive: Word the label so that checked means yes. Avoid negatives that make unchecked a double negative.
  - Do: Email me product updates; I agree to the terms
  - Avoid: Don't email me
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#visible-label: Provide a visible label that names the value. Placeholder text is not a label.
  - Do: Email address
  - Avoid: Enter email
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#hint-adds-information: Use a hint only for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-says-what-to-fix: Write the error as what to fix.
  - Do: Enter an email address with an @ sign
  - Avoid: Invalid
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#explain-disabled: When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.

### Behavior

- **MUST** toggle-on-activate: Clicking the box or the label, or pressing Space on the focused box, toggles checked and fires input then change.
- **MUST** indeterminate-clears-on-activate: Activating an indeterminate checkbox clears indeterminate and toggles checked.
- **MUST** indeterminate-not-a-value: Indeterminate does not change checked or the submitted value.
- **MUST** programmatic-no-events: Setting checked or indeterminate from script does not fire input or change.
- **SHOULD** form-value: When checked, the value submits under the name. Unchecked submits nothing. Reset restores the initial checked state and clears indeterminate.
  - Extends: pattern.form-field#form-value
  - Applies when: The control belongs to a form.
- **MUST** required-blocks-submit: A required checkbox that is unchecked blocks its form from submitting.
  - Extends: pattern.form-field#required-blocks-submit
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-marks-invalid: A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
- **SHOULD** pattern.form-field#clear-error: Clear the error when the person edits the value, and on form reset, which restores the value but leaves the error.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit: While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-prevents-interaction: Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#disabled-submits-nothing: A disabled control submits nothing.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** mixed-state: Indeterminate is exposed to assistive technology as mixed.
- **MUST** not-color-alone: Checked and indeterminate are shown by the indicator's shape, not by fill color alone.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone
- **MUST** forced-colors: Under forced colors, the box outline, the indicator, and focus stay visible in every state.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#label-is-name: The visible label is the control's accessible name.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#described-by-hint-and-error: The hint and the error are associated with the control, so assistive technology reads them as its description.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#invalid-not-color-alone: The invalid state always includes the error text, so meaning never depends on color alone.
- **MUST** pattern.form-field#required-announced: A required control is announced as required, and shows it by more than color.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.

## Accessibility

- Role: Checkbox
- Name: Required from the visible label.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the checkbox. |
| Space | Toggle checked. |

## Rationale

- **Checkbox consumes semantic tokens directly.** Tokens ADR 0003. The checked fill reuses the primary action roles, whose on-action foreground is already audited against them. The box uses semantic.radius.compact, the radius for small controls. No component-token namespace.
- **Checked and indeterminate are states driven by their parameters.** They paint the box the same way and differ only in the indicator. When both are set, the box is indeterminate: it shows the dash, not the check mark, until activation clears indeterminate.
- **A checked or indeterminate box does not change on hover.** The filled box and its indicator already confirm the state. Hover strengthens the border of an unchecked, valid box only. The checked + hover and indeterminate + hover conditions keep the checked colors.
- **An invalid box keeps its danger border on hover and when checked.** The danger border is the visual link to the error message, so hover does not replace it. A checked or indeterminate invalid box keeps the primary fill with a danger border, so it shows both its value and its error.
- **Disabled replaces checked, indeterminate, and invalid colors, but not the indicator.** A disabled box uses disabled fill and border in every combination, and the indicator uses the disabled foreground. The indicator shape still shows whether it is checked or indeterminate.
- **Label, hint, and error belong to the checkbox.** Same decision as Text field. A separate field shell does not exist yet. Association stays on this control until that shell lands.
- **One size, no density variant, no pressed state.** The box is a square aligned to the first line of the label, and the mark fills it. Both sizes are in the token map as spacing primitives, because no semantic size role exists (tokens ADR 0003). The label row is the click target, so compact layouts change spacing around the checkbox, not the checkbox. Activation commits on release, so there is no separate pressed styling.
- **No icon-only, unlabeled, or visually hidden label.** The visible label is the accessible name and part of the click target, so every checkbox shows it, including one in a table row. Selecting rows with a checkbox whose label is not shown needs a row-selection pattern, which does not exist yet.
- **No loading state, nothing mirrors under right-to-left, and no animation.** Toggling is local until submit, so there is no work to wait on; settings that save immediately belong to Switch. The check mark and dash are not directional, and box and label order follows the inline direction. State changes swap colors and the indicator instantly, so there is nothing to reduce under a reduced-motion preference.
- **Checkbox groups are not part of this component.** Group a list under a visible group label that names the set. A group-level label and error belong to a field shell.

## Links

### alternative

- [Button](component.button) — Trigger an action by itself. Checkbox records a choice.
- [Radio group](component.radio-group) — Choose exactly one option from a list. Checkboxes are independent. Nothing stops two being checked.
- [Switch](component.switch) — Apply a setting as soon as it is toggled, with no submit. A checkbox value takes effect when its form is submitted.

### alternative-to

- [Radio group](component.radio-group) — Choose any number of independent options. Radio options are mutually exclusive.
- [Switch](component.switch) — Record an independent choice for later submission. Checkbox communicates a choice that takes effect on submit.

### follows

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Form field](pattern.form-field)

### related

- [Radio group](component.radio-group)
- [Switch](component.switch)
- [Text field](component.text-field)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-checkbox>`

### Import

```js
import { defineCheckbox } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/checkbox";

defineCheckbox();
```

### Usage

```html
<form>
  <ds-checkbox label="Email me product updates" name="updates" hint="About one email a month." checked></ds-checkbox>
  <ds-checkbox label="I agree to the terms" name="terms" required></ds-checkbox>
  <ds-button type="submit">Continue</ds-button>
</form>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | parameter `label` | string | Visible label. This is the accessible name. |
| `hint` | attribute | parameter `hint` | string | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |
| `error` | attribute | parameter `error` | string | What to fix. A non-empty value marks the control invalid and is included in the accessible description. |
| `checked` | attribute | parameter `checked` | boolean | Whether the option is on. The value given at creation is the initial state that reset restores. |
| `indeterminate` | attribute | parameter `indeterminate` | boolean | Shows a mixed state, for a parent whose options are partly selected. Presentational only; it does not change the submitted value. |
| `name` | attribute | parameter `name` | string | Form field name. The value is submitted under this name when checked. |
| `value` | attribute | parameter `value` | string | Value submitted when checked. Defaults to "on". |
| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean | Prevents toggling. A disabled checkbox does not submit its value. |
| `required` | attribute | parameter `required` | boolean | The checkbox must be checked before submit. Conveyed by more than color. |
| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. |
| `input` | event | event `input` |  | The checked state changed from user interaction. |
| `change` | event | event `change` |  | The checked state was committed from user interaction. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

### Forms

The `checked` attribute sets the initial state. Setting the `checked` property changes the current
state, and form reset restores the attribute's state. Without `value`, a checked checkbox submits
`on`, as a native checkbox does.

To validate in your own code, set `novalidate` on the form so the submit reaches your listener.
Read the values there, and set `error` on a checkbox that needs a correction. Clear `error` on its
`change` event and when the form resets, because a reset leaves it set.

### Groups

Group related checkboxes in a native `fieldset` with a `legend` that names the set:

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Notifications</legend>
  <ds-checkbox label="Product updates" name="notify" value="updates"></ds-checkbox>
  <ds-checkbox label="Security alerts" name="notify" value="security"></ds-checkbox>
</fieldset>
```

Every checkbox shows its `label`, including one in a table row. Do not hide the label with CSS.

### Select all

Give the parent checkbox no `name`, so it submits nothing. Set its `checked` property when every
option is on and its `indeterminate` property when only some are. On its `change` event, set the
`checked` property of each option. Setting these from script fires no events
(`component.checkbox#programmatic-no-events`), so update the parent yourself when an option changes.

# Button

Use Button to trigger an action or to submit or reset a form.

Triggers an action or submits or resets a form.

## When to use

- Trigger an action in the current view.
- Submit or reset a form.

## When not to use

- Navigate to another location. Use [Link](component.link) instead. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.
- Display status or metadata. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Button communicates an available action.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control | interactive-surface | Interactive control. |
| content | label | Action label with an optional decorative icon. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | enum | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive` | `primary` |  |
| size | enum | `small`, `medium` | `medium` |  |
| action | enum | `activate`, `submit`, `reset` | `activate` |  |
| disabled | boolean |  | `false` |  |
| fullWidth | boolean |  | `false` | Fills the available inline size. |
| accessibleName | string |  |  | Accessible name when visible content is insufficient. |

`variant` values:

- `primary`: Highest-emphasis action. Example: Save changes Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#primary)
- `secondary`: Supporting action. Example: Cancel Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#secondary)
- `tertiary`: Low-emphasis action. Example: View details Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#tertiary)
- `destructive`: Destructive or difficult-to-reverse action. Example: Delete project Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#destructive)

`size` values:

- `small`: Small button.
- `medium`: Medium button.

`action` values:

- `activate`: Triggers an action.
- `submit`: Submits the associated form.
- `reset`: Resets the associated form.

## Events

- `activate`: Requests the action represented by the button.

## States

`disabled`, `pressed`, `hover`, `focus`, `default`

## Preferences

- `reducedMotion`: `reduce`

## Rules

Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **MUST** label-describes-result: Use a concise label that describes the result.
  - Do: Save changes; Delete account
  - Avoid: Click here
- **MUST** destructive-for-risky-actions: Use the destructive variant only for destructive or difficult-to-reverse actions.
- **SHOULD** explain-disabled: When the context does not say why an action is disabled, say why near it.
- **SHOULD** follow-action-hierarchy: Apply the action hierarchy pattern when several actions appear together.
  - See: pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis

### Behavior

- **MUST** disabled-prevents-activation: Disabled prevents activation.
- **SHOULD** explicit-form-action: In a form, set action to submit or reset when the button should submit or reset. The default activate does neither.
- **SHOULD** form-submit-reset: Submit submits the button's form, and reset restores that form's initial values.
  - Applies when: The button belongs to a form.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** icon-accessible-name: Icon-only buttons have an accessible name.
- **MUST** forced-colors: Under forced colors, emphasis stays visible: primary and destructive are filled, secondary is outlined, and tertiary is text alone. A disabled button stays distinguishable from an enabled one.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.

## Accessibility

- Role: Button
- Name: Required from visible content or accessibleName.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to or from the button. |
| Enter | Activate. |
| Space | Activate. |

## Rationale

- **Button reads semantic tokens directly and has no component-token namespace.** Its component tokens only restated the semantic tier, so they added names without adding a customization boundary (tokens ADR 0003).

## Links

### alternative

- [Badge](component.badge) — Display status or metadata. Button communicates an available action.
- [Link](component.link) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.

### alternative-to

- [Avatar](component.avatar) — Open a profile or account menu by pressing the avatar. Avatar is not a control. Place it inside a Button or a Link, which give the action its role, focus, and accessible name.
- [Badge](component.badge) — Trigger an action in the current view. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action.
- [Card](component.card) — Make a large target that only triggers one action or navigates, with no content of its own. A control styled as a card hides its role. Use Button for an action, or Link for navigation, and let the card hold content.
- [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Trigger an action by itself. Checkbox records a choice.
- [Icon](component.icon) — Trigger an action with an icon alone. Icon is not a control. A button with an icon and an accessible name gives the action semantics and focus.
- [Link](component.link) — Trigger an action or submit a form. Buttons provide action semantics and form behavior.
- [Text field](component.text-field) — Trigger an action by itself. Text field collects a value.

### composes

- [Icon](component.icon)

### follows

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis)
- `parameters.variant.destructive` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#destructive)
- `parameters.variant.primary` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#primary)
- `parameters.variant.secondary` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#secondary)
- `parameters.variant.tertiary` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#tertiary)

### related

- [Spinner](component.spinner)
- [Tooltip](component.tooltip)
- [Settings action hierarchy](example.action-hierarchy.settings)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

### used-in

- [Alert](component.alert)
- [Dialog](component.dialog)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-button>`

### Import

```js
import { defineButton } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/button";

defineButton();
```

### Usage

```html
<ds-button variant="primary">Save changes</ds-button>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | attribute | parameter `variant` | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive` |  |
| `size` | attribute | parameter `size` | `small`, `medium` |  |
| `type` | attribute | parameter `action` | `activate` → `button`, `submit`, `reset` |  |
| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean |  |
| `full-width` | attribute | parameter `fullWidth` | boolean | Fills the available inline size. |
| `aria-label` | attribute | parameter `accessibleName` | string | Accessible name when visible content is insufficient. |
| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. |
| `click` | event | event `activate` |  | Requests the action represented by the button. |

A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.

### Forms

Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set the type when it participates in a form:

```html
<form>
  <!-- form fields -->
  <ds-button type="button" variant="secondary">Cancel</ds-button>
  <ds-button type="submit" variant="primary">Save changes</ds-button>
</form>
```

Use `type="reset"` only when restoring every form control to its initial value is the intended
behavior.

### Styles

Do not recreate Button states with product CSS. Use the published variants and sizes first. Treat
`::part(button)` as an escape hatch that requires a specific product need and design review.

### Icons

Mark a decorative icon hidden from assistive technology. Provide `aria-label` when an icon is the
only visible content.

### Why `aria-label` and not `label`

Button maps `accessibleName` to `aria-label`, while Icon, Spinner, and Tabs map it to `label`. The
difference is deliberate. `aria-label` is the attribute people already put on an icon-only button,
and Button only passes it to the native button inside, so it keeps its standard meaning. The other
three use `label` because their name does more than name: Icon is hidden from assistive technology
without one, Spinner falls back to "Loading", and Tabs names the tab list inside it rather than the
host. They set the name through `ElementInternals` or on that inner element, so the host never
gains `aria-*` attributes. Renaming either side would break published markup.
